sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda Drought Hazard Assessment and Mapping: Summary Report
sources.organization: Organization of American States / USAID Caribbean Disaster Mitigation Project
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical drought impacts and watershed conditions assessed in a 2001 technical summary.
sources.methodology: OAS hazard-mapping summary draws on secondary records, maps, consultations and limited field observations.
sources.limitations: The report is dated; rainfall and watershed data were limited, and it does not attribute drought impacts to anthropogenic climate change.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda Inland Flood Hazard Mapping: Summary Report
sources.organization: Organization of American States / USAID Caribbean Disaster Mitigation Project
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical flood susceptibility and settlement conditions summarized in 2001.
sources.methodology: OAS technical summary maps inland flood hazards and describes watershed, soil, drainage and settlement factors.
sources.limitations: The maps were preliminary because rainfall, watershed and drainage data were limited; findings are not a current risk assessment.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda: Rapid Needs Assessment following Hurricane Irma
sources.organization: Government of Antigua and Barbuda, with World Bank/GFDRR, United Nations and European Union
sources.temporal_coverage: Post-disaster damage, loss and recovery needs after Hurricanes Irma and Maria in September 2017.
sources.methodology: Joint government-partner recovery needs assessment; this source is its executive summary.
sources.limitations: Assessment records disaster impacts and recommended needs, not subsequent completion of recovery measures.

sources.title: Concluding observations on the combined fourth to seventh periodic reports of Antigua and Barbuda
sources.organization: United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women
sources.temporal_coverage: Committee observations following its 20 February 2019 review; includes consequences of Hurricane Irma and recovery concerns.
sources.methodology: Treaty-body concluding observations based on the State review and information considered by the Committee.
sources.limitations: The observations identify concerns and recommendations; they are not a quantitative assessment of all affected women or recovery outcomes.

sources.title: Capacity Building for Improved Transparency of Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation in Antigua and Barbuda: Terminal Review
sources.organization: United Nations Environment Programme / Global Environment Facility
sources.temporal_coverage: Terminal evaluation of the 2019–2024 CBIT project, with primary review work in October–November 2025.
sources.methodology: Full terminal review assesses project outputs, outcomes, performance and sustainability using document review and stakeholder evidence.
sources.limitations: This evaluates climate-data and reporting institutions, not household adaptation outcomes; sustainability ratings are evaluative judgments.

sources.title: National Adaptation Plan: Sectoral Adaptation Plans and Local Area Adaptation Plans
sources.organization: Department of Environment, Government of Antigua and Barbuda
sources.temporal_coverage: Government announcement on 8 July 2026 of national, sectoral and local adaptation plans.
sources.methodology: Department of Environment webpage summarizes the NAP, sectoral plans and named local planning areas.
sources.limitations: The announcement describes plans and participation, not implementation, financing or measured resilience outcomes.

claims.locator: Summary report, section 'Drought Impacts', 1983–84 Antigua drought
claims.paraphrase: The report records crop damage and livestock deaths during Antigua's 1983 drought; some households lacked piped water for months and hotels trucked water.
claims.limitations: This is a historical event account, not evidence of current water access or attribution to climate change.

claims.locator: Summary report, Antigua watershed ranking and watershed 27–46 description
claims.paraphrase: OAS ranked watershed 27–46, southeast between English Harbour and St. James's Club, at very high drought risk, citing low rainfall, shallow soils, slopes, wind exposure and degraded slopes with many goats near Nelson's Dockyard National Park.
claims.limitations: The ranking reflects data available to the 2001 assessment and is not a current watershed measurement.

claims.locator: Summary report, Barbuda drought vulnerability discussion
claims.paraphrase: The report identifies flat lands around and south of Codrington as Barbuda's highest drought-risk area and notes groundwater dependence alongside aquifer concerns from sand mining.
claims.limitations: The assessment is from 2001 and does not quantify current aquifer condition or sand-mining effects.

claims.locator: Summary report, flood impacts and Cook Creek floodplain description
claims.paraphrase: The OAS summary identifies housing on the Cook Creek floodplain as exposed; during Hurricane Lenny, floodwater floated houses whose ground floors were about one metre above grade.
claims.limitations: This is a historical site example; the summary does not establish present housing conditions or recurrence probability.

claims.paraphrase: The report says shallow, low-permeability soils and rapid drainage combine with sealed urban surfaces and grazing-related soil compaction to increase runoff and flood vulnerability.
claims.limitations: The summary describes contributing conditions but does not quantify their separate effects or provide updated local measurements.

claims.locator: Executive summary, PDF p. 4, Barbuda housing damage
claims.paraphrase: The post-disaster assessment reports that 642 of Barbuda's 670 houses were damaged, and that 95% of the housing stock was damaged, with 45% uninhabitable.
claims.limitations: Damage estimates refer to the immediate 2017 post-disaster assessment and are not current housing counts.

claims.locator: Executive summary, PDF p. 4, water and sanitation damage
claims.paraphrase: The assessment reports that all Barbuda water sources were affected: the desalination plant flooded, pipes were damaged, cisterns were polluted, and groundwater faced surface contamination and saltwater intrusion.
affected_groups: households dependent on cisterns and groundwater
claims.limitations: The summary reports 2017 damage and immediate needs; it does not document later repair status.

claims.locator: Executive summary, PDF pp. 5–6, education and social infrastructure
claims.paraphrase: The assessment says damaged schools and childcare facilities on Barbuda left students displaced to Antigua while education services were restored.
claims.limitations: The summary describes post-Irma displacement and damage, not present school access or the duration of displacement.

claims.paraphrase: CEDAW states that Irma led to evacuation of Barbuda's entire population to Antigua and that women and girls continued to face education, health and livelihood challenges.
affected_groups: women and girls displaced from Barbuda
claims.limitations: The Committee describes challenges reported in its 2019 review; this is not evidence that all challenges persisted after that date.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: CEDAW explicitly links Hurricane Irma with evacuation of Barbuda's population and continuing gendered education, health and livelihood challenges (para. 9).

claims.paraphrase: CEDAW warns that post-disaster land redistribution decisions could deprive women of communal land ownership and recommends women's participation in recovery and land decisions, including for women in agriculture and fisheries.
affected_groups: older women and women with disabilities
claims.limitations: This is a Committee concern and recommendation; it does not establish the eventual land-allocation outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: CEDAW places its concern about women's communal-land rights in the context of post-Irma recovery and evacuation (paras. 9–10).

claims.locator: Terminal review, PDF pp. 71–72, paragraph 150 and outcome assessment
claims.paraphrase: The UNEP terminal review rates outcome 1 largely achieved: the Environment Registry was developed, launched and operational, and stakeholders reported its use for greenhouse-gas inventory and broader climate MRV work.
claims.limitations: The review assesses institutional MRV capacity, not whether the system has reduced local climate vulnerability.

claims.locator: Terminal review, PDF pp. 83–85 and paragraphs 291, 306–307
claims.paraphrase: The review finds financial sustainability moderately unlikely because recurring Registry maintenance funding is unsecured, technical support remains external, and integration with the Ministry of Finance is limited.
affected_groups: government agencies relying on climate data
claims.limitations: This is the terminal review's institutional sustainability judgment, not a measured interruption in climate services.

claims.locator: Terminal review, PDF pp. 98–99 and 83, system-wide adoption and sustainability
claims.paraphrase: The review says Registry tools are used within the Environment Department but adoption across government remains incomplete; it also identifies dependence on individual champions and risks from staff turnover and shifting priorities.
claims.limitations: The evaluation describes risks to institutional continuity; it does not document specific service failures caused by these constraints.

claims.locator: Department of Environment NAP announcement, Local Area Adaptation Plans
claims.paraphrase: The government says Local Area Adaptation Plans were prepared for the City of St. John's, Airport/Fitches Creek, and the Jolly Harbour–Johnsons Point area.
affected_groups: residents and stakeholders in named planning areas
claims.limitations: The webpage announces plans but does not provide their full text or evidence of implementation and results.

claims.locator: Department of Environment NAP announcement, stakeholder participation
claims.paraphrase: The Department reports that stakeholders helped shape the sectoral and local plans and select their strategies and interventions.
affected_groups: stakeholders in local and sectoral planning
claims.limitations: The announcement does not identify participants by group or establish the degree of influence over final plan decisions.

search_audit.query: Antigua Barbuda named local drought flood vulnerability watershed Codrington Cook Creek OAS report
search_audit.outcome: Opened OAS drought and flood summaries and the 2017 recovery assessment; found historical watershed, Cook Creek, Codrington, housing and water-system examples, but no current household-scale risk map in the opened texts.

search_audit.query: Antigua Barbuda Hurricane Irma displacement women communal land access post disaster CEDAW
search_audit.outcome: CEDAW explicitly links Irma with evacuation from Barbuda and gendered service and livelihood challenges, and raises a post-disaster communal-land rights concern; no source found an armed-conflict or violence pathway tied to climate hazards.

search_audit.query: Antigua Barbuda climate adaptation disaster recovery insecurity conflict impeding services climate projects
search_audit.outcome: No country-specific primary source found that conflict or insecurity impeded climate adaptation or disaster services; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

search_audit.query: Antigua Barbuda local adaptation plan climate registry capacity climate risk map disaster risk reduction
search_audit.outcome: Opened the government NAP announcement and UNEP terminal review, which document named local planning areas and climate-reporting capacity; the review also identifies unresolved financing and cross-government continuity constraints.

gaps: No existing ATG country baseline was present in the assigned worktree.

The full 2025 National Adaptation Plan was inaccessible because the UNFCCC retrieval timed out and the government-hosted PDF exceeded the full-text extraction limit; no claims rely on its search excerpts.
The OAS drought and flood summaries date from 2001 and should be treated as historical evidence, not current local risk measurements.
CEDAW's displacement and land-rights concerns are Committee findings/recommendations; they do not establish later land-allocation outcomes or an armed-conflict pathway.
No country-specific evidence was found that conflict or insecurity has disrupted climate adaptation or climate-service delivery; this remains a search gap.
The UNEP review documents climate-data institutions rather than household resilience, and identifies unresolved financial and cross-government sustainability risks.
